study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states research objectives. (1) Research hypotheses/questions are provided: The study aims to quantitatively estimate neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a novel framework integrating normative model and NMF from a dimensional perspective. (2) The purpose of applying normative modeling is described: to obtain subject-level differences in gray matter morphometry, parse them into latent disease factors, capture sources of clinical heterogeneity, reconcile group-level and subject-level findings, and identify putative OCD subtypes for precision medicine. Both criteria are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "To quantitatively estimate the heterogeneity of OCD, we proposed a novel framework integrating the normative model and non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) from a dimensional perspective." | "Our findings suggest that morphological differences of individuals with OCD are the unique combination of distinct neuroanatomical patterns. The proposed framework quantitatively estimating neuroanatomical heterogeneity paves the way for precision medicine in OCD."
